thesis: QQQ is the most concentrated way to own the same AI trade we already hold directly in NVDA, MSFT, AMZN and AAPL, and it is the weakest-looking chart in the book: RSI 42, 3m momentum +2.1%, score +0.37. Buying the Nasdaq nine days before an FOMC where a hike is roughly a coin flip, on top of positions that already carry that exposure, is paying costs to double up.
bull_case: The long-term trend has not broken - packet close 718.96 with close > SMA50 > SMA200 - and ATR of 1.1% makes it one of the cheapest positions to hold in volatility terms. The underlying earnings have been strong this cycle: Microsoft's Azure accelerated to +43% constant currency, Amazon's AWS grew 37%, and Nvidia guided to $108B. August payrolls at +162k against +53k expected describe an economy that is not rolling over. Waller said on 3 Sep he was inclined to hold rates at 3.5-3.75%, so the hawkish outcome is not settled.
bear_case: Momentum is already gone: +2.1% over three months and RSI 42 make QQQ the weakest of our equity holdings, and it is drifting while the megacaps inside it make headlines. The rate picture is actively hostile - the 2-year hit its highest since January 2025 and the 10-year moved to ~4.8% after the 4 Sep payrolls print, with fed funds futures putting a hike at 58-66% for 15-16 Sep. Concentration is the real objection: AI-linked names are roughly 40-45% of S&P 500 cap and more of the Nasdaq-100, so QQQ is not diversification on top of our single-name AI book - it is the same bet with a fee. September is also the weakest month seasonally, and the energy-driven inflation impulse from the Iran conflict argues the Fed's hand is being forced.
catalysts: 15-16 Sep 2026 FOMC decision and dot plot
August CPI ahead of the FOMC
risks: Hawkish hike on 16 Sep with the 10-year through 5%
Overlapping exposure: QQQ duplicates NVDA, MSFT, AMZN and AAPL risk
RSI 42 and +2.1% 3m momentum: the trend is stalling
September seasonality and the energy-led inflation impulse
invalidation: Flips long on a weekly close above 745 after the 16 Sep FOMC, which would be a new high made through the event rather than before it; the bear case confirms on a close below 690, breaking the SMA50 and the summer range.
